name: Hosts, Files & Software
description: Attack-surface inventory: who is talking on the wire, what software they run, and which files crossed the network. Pair with the Security Posture tab for exposure context.

charts.title: Active Hosts (Packet Counts)
charts.description: Hosts ranked by packet volume. Top talkers are usually the priority pivots for investigation: noisy clients, busy servers and unmonitored infra appear here.

charts.title: Device Manufacturers
charts.description: OUI-derived hardware vendors of devices observed on the LAN. Unexpected vendors (consumer gear in a server VLAN, IoT in a corporate net) point to rogue or shadow-IT devices.

charts.title: Software Products Detected
charts.description: Inventory of software products fingerprinted on the wire (banners, headers, TLS, DPI). Cross-reference with the Vulnerability records to spot exposed versions.

charts.title: Software With Known Vulnerabilities
charts.description: Share of detected software linked to at least one CVE in our local database. A high true-share is a strong signal that the environment is not patched.

charts.title: Extracted File Types (Magika)
charts.description: File-content categories detected by Google Magika across extracted artifacts. Executables, scripts or archives appearing on unexpected channels (mail, HTTP) deserve attention.

charts.title: Windows Executables on the Wire
charts.description: Share of extracted files identified as Windows PE binaries. Any non-zero share warrants a hash check against malware reputation services.
